title: Wringer acceptance evidence
description: `acceptance.json` — a sibling file in a `wring verify` bundle, present ONLY when an APPROVED `wringer.spec.yaml` declares criteria. It answers, per criterion, whether the record evidences it. `evidenced` is deliberately hard: the bound gate must have passed in this run AND the repo's record must show that gate can fail, because a gate born green has never demonstrated it can tell satisfied from unsatisfied. Absent from every bundle whose repo has not opted in, so existing readers are untouched.

schema_version.description: Identifies the artifact format a reader is holding.

counts.description: One key per state, always all five. These are counts over an ENUMERATED population — the criteria the approved spec declares — so a zero here is a real zero rather than the invented one the absence law forbids elsewhere.

criteria.description: In the order the approved spec declares them. Nothing here is sorted by state: a ranking of criteria would be this artifact deciding which debts matter, which is the reader's call.

criterion.description: The criterion id, exactly as written in `wringer.spec.yaml`. The join key — never slugged or normalised, because a normalised join is a silent mis-bind.

required.description: From the spec. Only a required criterion can refuse delivery, and only when it is also bound.

state.description: `evidenced` — bound, passed this run, and the record shows the gate can fail. `unevidenced` — unbound, or bound but born green. `gate-failed` — the gate ran and failed, so the criterion is not met: the ordinary honest state of work in progress. `gate-did-not-run` — bound, but no result in this bundle (skipped, interrupted); absence is absence, never a pass-through to an older green. `human` — answered by people, and nothing here scored it.

gate.description: The gate whose `proves:` names this criterion, or null when nothing binds it. Null is a DEBT, not an error: criteria default to required and nothing is bound the moment a spec is approved.

command.description: The bound gate's command, after redaction. Null when unbound or human. Identity for the discrimination record is `(gate id, command)`: edit the command and the history resets, because editing is how checks narrow.

receipt.description: Where the record shows this gate can fail. Null for every state except `evidenced`, and null WITH a reason rather than an empty object — a receipt that names nothing would be the claim this artifact exists to refuse.

kind.description: `failure` — a recorded genuine failure of this exact pair (not a timeout, not exit 127). `sensitive` — a `--prove` pass recorded it failing on the pre-change tree while passing on the changed one.

bundle.description: Repo-relative path to the bundle holding the receipt, so a reader can go and look.

cites.description: PRESENT ONLY on a `sensitive` receipt: the line the sensitivity rests on, carried verbatim from `vacuity.json`. Load-bearing rather than decorative — a sensitivity receipt inherits vacuity's blind spot, so a gate whose own command arrived with the change reads sensitive for that reason alone, and this line is how a reader tells. Deliberately NOT classified here: SPEC_VACUITY §4b's law is to make the failure visible, never to auto-classify it.

reason.description: Why this state, in words a person can act on — including the one-run remedy when a gate is born green.

refuses.description: Whether this row stops `wring deliver`. True only for a criterion that is both REQUIRED and BOUND and not `evidenced`. An unbound criterion never refuses: binding a gate is the act that says 'hold me to this', and refusing without it would refuse the first delivery in every repo that ever ran `wring spec`.

limits.description: What this artifact does NOT say, travelling with the numbers rather than living in a spec nobody opened. Four entries at minimum, each pinned by content — including that a sensitivity receipt says the gate's result differed between two trees, not that the difference was the change.
